clue.text: Buddy and Charlie don't know the words?

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
you hum a tune when you don't know its lyrics

explanation.surface: A question about a friend called Charlie who can only mumble along to songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A buddy and a chum are both informal synonyms for a close friend.

clue.text: Passing mention of sex in broken Yoruba

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the rearranged letters
broken means the letters of the word Yoruba are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: IT is an old euphemism for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone notes a reference to sex made in halting Yoruba, a Nigerian language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like 'in passing', but here it means death. 'broken' rearranges the language's name to OBUARY, and 'in' sets the euphemism for sex inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper notice of someone's death is a mention made of their passing, i.e. their dying.

clue.text: Rookie Conservative, upside down and back to front

indicators.note: back to front here means the last letter is brought round to the front
in a down clue, upside down means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A novice Conservative politician is in a complete muddle, flipped every which way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside down' turns TORY into YROT; 'back to front' then brings its back letter T to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms for a beginner or novice who is new to something.

clue.text: Six ducks living on Scottish islands, one with more than one tongue

definitions.text: one with more than one tongue

indicators.note: on places the first piece before the islands in this down answer
ducks means dodges out, so those letters drop out of the word living

parts.note: the word living is taken as written before letters are removed
VI is six in Roman numerals
North and South Uist are islands of the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: Six ducks live in the Hebrides, and one of them can quack in several languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' takes VI out of LIVING to leave LING. North and South Uist are islands in Scotland's Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue here means a language, so someone who speaks several is a polyglot.

clue.text: Chemist stocks drug for stars

indicators.note: stocks means the shop holds the drug inside it

parts.note: Boots is a big British chain of chemist's shops
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A pharmacy keeps a drug on its shelves that is used by celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a big British chain of chemist's shops (pharmacies).
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a northern constellation, the Herdsman, a group of stars.

clue.text: Shadowy figure trashing hotel suite

indicators.note: trashing means wrecking, so the letters of hotel and suite are thrown about

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure is seen wrecking a hotel room, rock-star style.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline filled in black against a light background is a shadowy form of a person or thing.

clue.text: Friend tied knot round wattle

indicators.note: round means turned round, so the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to tie the knot is to marry, so tied knot means wed

explanation.surface: A friend gets married under a wattle tree, the Australian acacia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns PALWED back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A wattle is a fold of skin hanging from the throat, as on a turkey; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: American female tennis legend

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A tribute to a great American woman tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a woman, but the legend is Arthur, a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur, the first black man to win Wimbledon, is a famous player of the sport.

clue.text: Mate rounded Cape unnoticed

indicators.note: unnoticed means that letter goes missing, slipping away from the word

parts.note: chubby means plump and rounded in shape
C is an abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A sailor sailed round a headland without anyone noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounded' looks like sailing round the Cape; it is an adjective meaning plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate in the sense of spouse; this is an informal word for a husband.

clue.text: They worship former Tory leader, full of lies or nonsense

indicators.note: full of means the leader's initials hold the other letters inside

parts.note: IDS is Iain Duncan Smith, leader of the UK Conservative Party 2001-03

indicators.note: nonsense signals that the letters of lies and or are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fans of an ex-Conservative chief, whose speeches were full of untruths or rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: IDS (Iain Duncan Smith) led the Conservatives in 2001-03. 'nonsense' jumbles LIESOR into OLISER.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who adore or venerate someone are said to worship them; the answer is the noun for such people.

clue.text: Had better drug previously, it seemed to Arachne

indicators.note: previously puts the drug before the other piece

parts.note: meth is short for methamphetamine
ought, like had better, says what someone should do

explanation.surface: A warning that someone should have taken a drug earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: Arachne is the setter, so 'it seemed to Arachne' means 'it seemed to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb form meaning it seemed to me, used here of the setter herself.

clue.text: Split from husband, heading off to give birth in cowshed

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is lost

parts.note: a cow gives birth to a calf, i.e. calves

explanation.surface: A woman leaves her husband and goes off to have a baby in a cowshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the C from CALVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something into two equal parts is to split it.

clue.text: Grey matter with a laminated cover

indicators.note: the words with a laminated cover the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: Something grey comes with a plastic-coated cover.
explanation.definitionFit: These paired masses deep in the brain are made of grey matter, the nerve-cell tissue.

clue.text: Ram's purpose, in sum

parts.note: to expresses purpose, as in 'in order to'
a tup is a ram, the male sheep

explanation.surface: A question about what a ram is for, put in brief.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, 'Ram's purpose' is to tup, i.e. to mate with ewes.
explanation.definitionFit: To add up figures is to total them, the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Styptic band inserted into a temporary splint

indicators.note: inserted into means the band goes inside the splint

parts.note: a stent is a tube placed in a vessel to hold it open
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A medical scene: a bandage applied inside a temporary support.
explanation.definitionFit: A styptic stops bleeding by contracting tissue, which is what this kind of substance does.

clue.text: Cold meal wrapped in foil

indicators.note: wrapped means the meal is folded round the letter

parts.note: supper is an evening meal
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Leftover supper is kept cold under kitchen foil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' looks like kitchen wrap; it is a verb meaning thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart or ruin someone's plans; both words are verb synonyms for wrecking a scheme.

clue.text: Esteemed journalist is buried under grass

indicators.note: in a down answer the journalist goes beneath the grass

parts.note: a grass is an informer, as is a rat
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A respected reporter has died and lies beneath the turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly regarded; to be well thought of is to be valued by others.

clue.text: Date of road tax moving forward

indicators.note: moving forward means the tax piece is brought to the front

parts.note: ST is an abbreviation for street, a road
to tax someone's patience is to try it

explanation.surface: An official note about when car tax is due going forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret meeting between lovers is a romantic date, an assignation.

clue.text: Mo's audible nervous habit

indicators.note: audible means we want the word as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a mo and a tick are both informal words for a moment

explanation.surface: Someone called Mo has a nervous habit that others can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch or habitual spasm, especially of the face, is a nervous habit.

clue.text: A centre for research into breadfruit

indicators.note: into means those pieces go inside the money

parts.note: bread is slang for money, cash
a lab is a laboratory, a research centre

explanation.surface: A laboratory studying breadfruit, the tropical starchy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breadfruit' looks like one word but splits: 'bread' is CASH and 'fruit' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a gourd, the hard-shelled fruit of a tropical tree or vine.

clue.text: Perfectly embodies the ultimate in courageous soldier material

indicators.note: embodies means the phrase holds the next letter in its body

parts.note: to a T means perfectly

indicators.note: the ultimate in means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Praise for a brave soldier who embodies courage perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are thin strips of toast for dipping in a boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Grilled bread is what egg-dipping strips are cut from, so it is their material.

clue.text: You can count on these four Swedes swearing out loud

indicators.note: out loud tells us the phrase is spoken and heard as one word

parts.note: ABBA were the four-member Swedish pop group; cusses means swears

explanation.surface: A Swedish pop quartet cursing, and you can rely on them.
explanation.definitionFit: These are frames with sliding beads used for counting, so you literally count on them.

clue.text: Do successors occupy country, having ousted last PM?

indicators.note: occupy means the notes move in and sit inside the country
having ousted last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
in sol-fa the notes after do are re and mi

explanation.surface: A political question: will the next people take over the nation after the last PM is kicked out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the first note of the sol-fa scale, followed by re and mi.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister is also called the first minister, the head of government.

clue.text: Ends of Rice, Brown and Garner? Time for anger

indicators.note: ends of means the final letter of each of the three names

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A list of three surnames, then a call that time's up for fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone furious; both words are verbs meaning to provoke rage.

clue.text: Hit squire near the knuckle

indicators.note: hit suggests the word squire is knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A country gentleman is struck near his finger joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near the knuckle' is a British idiom for slightly indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly rude or indecent; the idiom and the borrowed French word are synonyms.

clue.text: Lure fish in a westerly direction and downwind

indicators.note: in an across clue westward is right to left, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to draw someone is to lure them
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler casts a lure westwards, with the wind behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The side away from the wind, sheltered; the nautical term for downwind.

clue.text: Show indifference and keep quiet, when confronted with wig

indicators.note: confronted with means placed face to face, the first piece just before the second

parts.note: sh is the call to keep quiet
rug is slang for a wig or toupee

explanation.surface: Faced with someone's toupee, you stay silent and act unbothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the shoulders is the gesture of not caring, a physical display of indifference.

clue.text: Most of matchmaker's meeting with male went smoothly

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is lost

parts.note: Swan Vestas is a well-known British brand of matches

explanation.surface: A matchmaker's meeting with a man went without a hitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matchmaker' looks like a romantic go-between; it is Swan, the British maker of Swan Vestas matches.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide along, as a swimmer does, is to move smoothly; the past tense suits went.

clue.text: People who undermine subordinates slyly, but noiselessly

indicators.note: slyly hints at the letters of subordinates being cunningly rearranged

parts.note: noiselessly means without din, a noise, so those letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Junior staff quietly and sneakily sabotage their bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: SUBORDINATES less D, I, N leaves SUBORATES, which 'slyly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Saboteurs deliberately wreck plans or equipment, undermining from within.

clue.text: Booze off limits to birth control enthusiast

indicators.note: off limits means the outer letters are taken away

parts.note: Marie Stopes was a pioneering British campaigner for birth control

explanation.surface: Alcohol is banned for a campaigner on contraception.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Stopes (1880-1958) opened Britain's first birth control clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning to drink alcohol heavily, as a toper does.

clue.text: Really big sizes are in the ascendant, OK?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the clothing size; plural sizes gives two
OS stands for outsize, the clothing size; plural sizes gives two

explanation.surface: Clothing in plus sizes is becoming more popular - is that acceptable?
explanation.definitionFit: Middling, neither good nor bad, just passable or all right.

clue.text: They went in search of sheepskin, as bottled gas ran out

definitions.text: They went in search of sheepskin

indicators.note: bottled is slang for drunk, so the letters reel about

explanation.surface: Someone bottled their gas supply, as the supply ran low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottled' seems to hold the gas; it is the anagram signal, and 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason's crew in Greek myth sailed in quest of the Golden Fleece, a ram's skin.

clue.text: Chat show host walks on water

definitions.meaning: the British TV interviewer Morgan, known by his first name
promenades built out over the sea, such as at Brighton

explanation.surface: A TV presenter thinks he can perform miracles.
explanation.definitionFit: A forename of a well-known talk-show host, and the plural of seaside walkways on stilts.
